# Summary: 

This notebook performs entity resolution over contributors and attempts to identify 
name variants of orgs and individuals as well as identify cases where different individuals
share the same name. 

The entity resolution process is designed to be compatible with what is already being done 
for the campaign finance data on the Voter Guide. The approach for the voter guide 
groups contributors by name to determine how much that contributor gave in aggregate. Known name
variants of individuals and orgs are mapped to a `Normalized` name in a Google Sheet.

The notebook uses name variant matching, fuzzy matching and a custom record linkage algorithm
to try to identify name variants. Name variants are manually reviewed and added to the map that
is also used for the Voter Guide. 

For this project, we are not classifying entities that gave less than $5k to a race/prop/pac,
so entity resolution / manual name variant review are only performed for entities that have 
the potential to cross this threshold. Entity resolution also focuses on within-race/pac 
contributions; not all name variants across all recipient committees are tracked since we 
aggregate within each prop/candidate race. 

Processing steps: 

(1) Download the latest 2026 name entity map (https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1THwQtvw5s9ZO9n7QHncekl4kRMc1Nf3MJHViSYALDps/edit?gid=897118445#gid=897118445) 
    and feedback from manual reviews of name variants (should already be in the directory).
(2) Run name variant linkage and fuzzy matching on all organizations. Surface potential name variants of organizations for manual review.
    After manual review is finished, new name variants are added to the 2026 name map. 
(3) Run record linkage algorithm on individuals to surface name variants for manual review AND surface potential cases
    of diferent individuals who share the same name. After manual review, add name variants and disambiguation cases to the
    2026 name map.

## Define helper functions

```{r}
# functions used in record linkage
safe_metaphone <- function(x) {
  clean <- str_replace_all(coalesce(x, ""), "[^A-Za-z]", "")
  ifelse(clean != "", metaphone(clean), NA_character_)
}

bigram_cosine <- function(a, b) stringsim(a, b, method = "cosine", q = 2)

# creates unique hash-based key for contributors
hash_id <- function(keys, prefix) {
  paste0(prefix, "_", substr(digest::digest(paste(sort(unique(keys)), collapse = "||"), algo = "xxhash32"), 1, 16))
}

# makes contributor_id
make_row_hash <- function(...) {
  cols <- list(...)
  n <- length(cols[[1]])
  vapply(seq_len(n), function(i) {
    parts <- vapply(cols, function(col) as.character(col[i]), character(1))
    digest::digest(paste(parts, collapse = "|"), algo = "xxhash32")
  }, character(1))
}

# recipient_key for applying threshold checks:
#   PAC contributions        -> Recipient.Committee.ID (each PAC evaluated separately)
#   ballot measure           -> name of Ballot.Measure (groups all committees for same measure/side)
#   candidate with Office    -> "Recipient.Name | Office" key for candidate race (Ben Allen has more than one committee)
add_recipient_key <- function(df) {
  df %>% mutate(
    recipient_key = case_when(
      coalesce(is_pac_contribution, FALSE)          ~ as.character(Recipient.Committee.ID),
      !is.na(Ballot.Measure) & Ballot.Measure != "" ~ Ballot.Measure,
      !is.na(Office) & Office != ""                 ~ paste(Recipient.Name, Office, sep = " | "),
      TRUE                                          ~ Recipient.Name
    )
  )
}

# look up contributor name in entity registry
# returns entity_id, is_conflict and is_new
lookup_cluster_uuid <- function(raw_names, mapping_df) {
  clean <- unique(toupper(raw_names))
  matched_uuids <- mapping_df %>%
    filter(raw_name %in% clean) %>%
    pull(entity_uuid) %>%
    unique()

  if (length(matched_uuids) == 0) {
    list(entity_id = UUIDgenerate(), is_conflict = FALSE, is_new = TRUE)
  } else if (length(matched_uuids) == 1) {
    list(entity_id = matched_uuids[1], is_conflict = FALSE, is_new = FALSE)
  } else {
    list(entity_id = matched_uuids[1], is_conflict = TRUE, is_new = FALSE)
  }
}
```

# Load PACs from previous run 

On the first run `pac_universe.csv` will be stale — it is generated in 0802b.
0802b runs the PAC graph over all PACs that contributed to the gov/IC race or one of the props.
`pac_universe.csv` include ALL PACs, regardless of contribution amount that are 
surfaced in the PAC graph in 0802b (all PACs indirectly connected to one of our 
prop/candidate committees). Matching algorithms are applied across all contributors to these PACs
to make sure we're properly aggregating all name variants of the same individual/organization.

```{r}
if (file.exists("08_outputs/pac_universe.csv")) {
  pac_universe     <- read.csv("08_outputs/pac_universe.csv", colClasses = "character")
  known_pacs       <- pac_universe %>% filter(as.logical(traversed))
  pac_contributors <- contributions_full %>%
    filter(Recipient.Committee.ID %in% known_pacs$pac_id)
  cat(sprintf("Loaded %d traversed PACs from pac_universe.csv (%d contributor rows)\n",
              nrow(known_pacs), nrow(pac_contributors)))
} else {
  known_pacs       <- data.frame(pac_id = character())
  pac_contributors <- contributions_full[0, ]
  cat("pac_universe.csv not found — run 0802b first, then re-run this notebook.\n")
}

# temporary fix to add pacs for props that were not previously being classified
if (file.exists("08_outputs/pac_universe_new_props.csv")) {
  pac_universe_new_props_raw <- read.csv("08_outputs/pac_universe_new_props.csv",
                                          colClasses = "character")
  pac_universe <- bind_rows(pac_universe, pac_universe_new_props_raw) %>%
    group_by(pac_id) %>%
    summarise(
      depth                      = min(as.integer(depth), na.rm = TRUE),
      is_seed                    = any(as.logical(is_seed),                    na.rm = TRUE),
      traversed                  = any(as.logical(traversed),                  na.rm = TRUE),
      has_pac_no_id_contributors = any(as.logical(has_pac_no_id_contributors), na.rm = TRUE),
      is_candidate_pac           = any(coalesce(as.logical(is_candidate_pac), FALSE)),
      is_federal_pac             = any(coalesce(as.logical(is_federal_pac),   FALSE)),
      .groups = "drop"
    )
}
```

# Combine direct and pac contributor data

Add PAC contributors to the `contributions` data to do entity resolution. 
It is possible a direct contributor can also be counted under PAC contributions
this happens when a ballot measure committee (e.g. YES ON 41 - CALIFORNIANS FOR TRANSPARENCY AND ACCOUNTABILITY, A COALITION OF SMALL BUSINESSES, TAXPAYERS, GOOD GOVERNMENT ADVOCATES, ACCOUNTANTS AND AUDITING EXPERTS)
contributes to a PAC. 

```{r}
n_direct <- nrow(contributions)
n_pac    <- nrow(pac_contributors)
contributions <- bind_rows(
  contributions    %>% mutate(is_pac_contribution = FALSE), # flag for distinguishing direct contributors from PAC contributors. direct wins
  pac_contributors %>% mutate(is_pac_contribution = TRUE)
) %>%
  distinct(rowid, .keep_all = TRUE)  # rowid is the source row number; both datasets share it b/c they are derived from contributions_full, so this drops PAC rows that duplicate a direct-contributor row
cat(sprintf("%d direct + %d pac → %d combined (%d duplicate rows dropped)\n",
            n_direct, n_pac, nrow(contributions),
            n_direct + n_pac - nrow(contributions)))
nrow(contributions)
```

## standardize employer + occupation for individuals

For individuals that are missing employer/occupation info, standardize employer/occupation to be `NONE` 
Note: there are edge cases where employer is N/A, but occupation indicates there are employed or self-employed. 
These individuals are tagged as major donors. 

```{r}
contributions <- contributions %>%
  mutate(
    standardized_employer_name   = if_else(entity_type == "individual" & standardized_employer_name == "", "NONE", standardized_employer_name),
    processed_employer_name  = if_else(entity_type == "individual" & processed_employer_name == "", "NONE", processed_employer_name),

    standardized_occupation  = if_else(entity_type == "individual" & standardized_occupation == "", "NONE", standardized_occupation),
    processed_occupation = if_else(entity_type == "individual" & processed_occupation == "", "NONE", processed_occupation),    
  )

```

# Update entity registry and no-link pairs

Syncs the 2026 Names CSV (used for normalization) and the name_entity_mapping.csv (tracks uuids per entity).
Dataset descriptions: 
`2026 Contributor name mapping and descriptions - Names.csv` : Official source of truth - maps record name to normalized name. Shared by the team. 
`entity_registry.csv` : keeps track of each canonical name that links name variants within an entity and the corresponding uuid.
`name_entity_mapping_rebuilt.csv` : essentially a copy of the Name 2026 data, but has a uuid for each row to keep track of unique entities (one uuid per `Normalized` name).
                                    updated manually with each review queue. 
`no_link_registry.csv` : feedback from each manual review. org names that were compared and determined not to be a link added to the registry.
                         note that only names w/in a review group are compared, may miss some name variants that weren't grouped in the same review group 
                         (which is why only names within a review group are added to the no-link registry).
                         
Download latest version of 2026 names map at: https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1THwQtvw5s9ZO9n7QHncekl4kRMc1Nf3MJHViSYALDps/edit?gid=897118445#gid=897118445 


```{r}
ENTITY_REGISTRY_PATH     <- here("08_inputs/entity_registry.csv") 
NAME_ENTITY_MAPPING_PATH <- here("08_inputs/name_entity_mapping_rebuilt.csv") # updated with each entity resolution review queue. 
NO_LINK_REGISTRY_PATH <- here("08_inputs/no_link_registry.csv")
registry_mtime <- if (file.exists(NO_LINK_REGISTRY_PATH)) file.mtime(NO_LINK_REGISTRY_PATH) else as.POSIXct(0, origin = "1970-01-01")

# only load feedback files newer than the registry's last write
# all historical files are loaded as a one-time backfill
NEW_ORG_FEEDBACK_FILES <- {
  f <- list.files(here("08_inputs"), pattern = "^org_name_variant_review_queue_w_review.*\\.csv$", full.names = TRUE)
  f[file.mtime(f) > registry_mtime]
}
NEW_INDIV_FEEDBACK_FILES <- {
  f <- list.files(here("08_inputs"), pattern = "^indiv_name_variant_review_queue_w_review.*\\.csv$", full.names = TRUE)
  f[file.mtime(f) > registry_mtime]
}

print(NEW_ORG_FEEDBACK_FILES)
print(NEW_INDIV_FEEDBACK_FILES)
```

```{r}
# official source of truth - shared by voter guide team 
names_2026 <- read.csv(
  here("08_inputs/2026 Contributor name mapping and descriptions - Names.csv"),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
) %>%
  rename(raw_name = Original, canonical_name = Normalized) %>% # rename columns so all dataframes share col names
  filter(!is.na(raw_name), raw_name != "", !is.na(canonical_name), canonical_name != "") %>%
  mutate(
    raw_name       = (toupper(raw_name)), 
    canonical_name = str_squish(canonical_name) # canonical name shouldn't have any double spaces
  )

# persistent UUID registry — updated by manual review (should be a copy of Names 2026, but tracks uuid)
if (file.exists(NAME_ENTITY_MAPPING_PATH)) {
  name_entity_mapping_existing <- read.csv(NAME_ENTITY_MAPPING_PATH, stringsAsFactors = FALSE) %>%
    mutate(confirmed = as.logical(confirmed))
} else {
  name_entity_mapping_existing <- tibble(raw_name = character(), entity_uuid = character(),
                                          canonical_name = character(), confirmed = logical(),
                                          added_date = character(), source = character())
}
```


```{r}
# create uuid lookup - matches canonical name to its uuid
canonical_uuid_conflicts <- name_entity_mapping_existing %>%
  filter(!is.na(canonical_name), confirmed == TRUE) %>%
  mutate(canonical_name = str_squish(canonical_name)) %>%
  group_by(canonical_name) %>%
  summarise(n_uuids = n_distinct(entity_uuid), uuids = paste(unique(entity_uuid), collapse = " | "), .groups = "drop") %>%
  filter(n_uuids > 1)

if (nrow(canonical_uuid_conflicts) > 0) {
  print(canonical_uuid_conflicts)
  stop(sprintf("%d canonical name(s) are mapped to more than one entity_uuid — resolve conflicts before proceeding.", nrow(canonical_uuid_conflicts)))
}

canonical_uuid_lookup <- name_entity_mapping_existing %>%
  filter(!is.na(canonical_name), confirmed == TRUE) %>%
  mutate(canonical_name = str_squish(canonical_name)) %>%
  distinct(canonical_name, entity_uuid) %>%
  select(canonical_name, entity_uuid)

# add uuids to any new entities added to the 2026 Names map (added by someone else on the team.)
canonical_uuid_map <- names_2026 %>%
  mutate(canonical_name = str_squish(canonical_name)) %>%
  distinct(canonical_name) %>%
  left_join(canonical_uuid_lookup, by = "canonical_name") %>% # join uuids to already known canonical names 
  mutate(entity_uuid = coalesce(entity_uuid, UUIDgenerate(n = n()))) # create new uuids for new canonical names

cat(sum(is.na(left_join(names_2026 %>% distinct(canonical_name),
                         canonical_uuid_lookup, by="canonical_name")$entity_uuid)),
    "new canonical groups in 2026 Names CSV assigned fresh UUIDs\n")

```

## Individual disambiguation subgroups

Contributors are aggregated based on their names; individual disambiguation separates individuals 
with the same name who have been manually confirmed to be different people by adding other variables
(employer, occupation, etc.) to the map and assigning a subgroup to these individuals. 

`subgroup_id` (A, B, C, etc.) distinguishes rows *within* one `canonical_name` — the same letter reused
under a different `canonical_name` is unrelated. Each confirmed `(canonical_name, subgroup_id)`
pair is a distinct person; give contributor their own persistent uuid, tracked in `name_entity_mapping.csv`
under a synthetic `canonical_name::subgroup_id` key. 

Records that don't match any subgroup's profile keep the plain canonical name uui.

```{r}
if (!"subgroup_id" %in% names(names_2026)) names_2026$subgroup_id <- NA_character_

subgroup_profiles <- names_2026 %>%
  filter(!is.na(subgroup_id), subgroup_id != "") %>%
  transmute(
    canonical_name     = canonical_name,
    subgroup_id        = as.character(subgroup_id),
    profile_employer   = na_if(toupper(str_squish(coalesce(Contributor.Employer, ""))), ""),
    profile_occupation = na_if(toupper(str_squish(coalesce(Contributor.Occupation, ""))), ""),
    profile_city       = na_if(toupper(str_squish(coalesce(Contributor.City, ""))), ""),
    profile_state      = na_if(toupper(str_squish(coalesce(Contributor.State, ""))), ""),
    profile_zip        = na_if(coalesce(as.character(Contributor.Zip.Code), ""), ""),
    profile_committee  = na_if(coalesce(as.character(Recipient.Committee.ID), ""), "")
  ) %>%
  distinct()

# assign a uuid per (canonical_name, subgroup_id)
subgroup_keys <- subgroup_profiles %>%
  distinct(canonical_name, subgroup_id) %>%
  mutate(raw_name = paste(canonical_name, subgroup_id, sep = "::"))

known_subgroup_uuids <- name_entity_mapping_existing %>%
  filter(source == "subgroup_disambig") %>%
  distinct(raw_name, entity_uuid)

new_subgroup_keys <- subgroup_keys %>%
  filter(!raw_name %in% known_subgroup_uuids$raw_name) %>%
  mutate(
    entity_uuid    = UUIDgenerate(n = n()),
    canonical_name = NA_character_, # composite key, not a real canonical name - excluded from the canonical/uuid checks above
    confirmed      = TRUE,
    added_date     = as.character(Sys.Date()),
    source         = "subgroup_disambig"
  ) %>%
  select(raw_name, entity_uuid, canonical_name, confirmed, added_date, source)

if (nrow(new_subgroup_keys) > 0) {
  name_entity_mapping_existing <- bind_rows(name_entity_mapping_existing, new_subgroup_keys)
  write.csv(name_entity_mapping_existing, NAME_ENTITY_MAPPING_PATH, row.names = FALSE)
  cat("Assigned", nrow(new_subgroup_keys), "new subgroup uuid(s) for disambiguated individuals\n")
}

subgroup_uuid_lookup <- bind_rows(
    known_subgroup_uuids,
    new_subgroup_keys %>% select(raw_name, entity_uuid)
  ) %>%
  separate(raw_name, into = c("canonical_name", "subgroup_id"), sep = "::", extra = "merge")
```

```{r}
# match a contribution record to a subgroup: it matches subgroup S if it agrees with AT LEAST
# ONE of S's profile rows on every field that row has filled in
# records matching more than one subgroup are left unresolved 
# records matching none keep the default canonical-name-level uuid
assign_subgroup_entity_id <- function(df, default_col = "entity_uuid") {
  if (nrow(subgroup_profiles) == 0) return(df)

  df <- df %>% mutate(.match_row_id = row_number())

  candidates <- df %>%
    filter(Normalized %in% subgroup_profiles$canonical_name) %>%
    transmute(
      .match_row_id,
      canonical_name  = Normalized,
      cand_employer   = toupper(str_squish(coalesce(Contributor.Employer, ""))),
      cand_occupation = toupper(str_squish(coalesce(Contributor.Occupation, ""))),
      cand_city       = toupper(str_squish(coalesce(Contributor.City, ""))),
      cand_state      = toupper(str_squish(coalesce(Contributor.State, ""))),
      cand_zip        = coalesce(as.character(Contributor.Zip.Code), ""),
      cand_committee  = coalesce(as.character(Recipient.Committee.ID), "")
    ) %>%
    inner_join(subgroup_profiles, by = "canonical_name", relationship = "many-to-many") %>%
    mutate(
      is_match =
        (is.na(profile_employer)   | profile_employer   == cand_employer)   &
        (is.na(profile_occupation) | profile_occupation == cand_occupation) &
        (is.na(profile_city)       | profile_city       == cand_city)       &
        (is.na(profile_state)      | profile_state       == cand_state)      &
        (is.na(profile_zip)        | profile_zip        == cand_zip)        &
        (is.na(profile_committee)  | profile_committee  == cand_committee)
    ) %>%
    filter(is_match) %>%
    distinct(.match_row_id, canonical_name, subgroup_id)

  ambiguous <- candidates %>%
    group_by(.match_row_id) %>%
    filter(n_distinct(subgroup_id) > 1) %>%
    ungroup()

  if (nrow(ambiguous) > 0) {
    warning(sprintf(
      "%d contribution record(s) matched more than one disambiguation subgroup -- left unresolved (default uuid used). Review:",
      n_distinct(ambiguous$.match_row_id)
    ))
    print(
      df %>% inner_join(ambiguous %>% distinct(.match_row_id), by = ".match_row_id") %>%
        select(Contributor.Name, Contributor.Employer, Contributor.Occupation,
               Contributor.City, Contributor.State, Contributor.Zip.Code, Recipient.Committee.ID)
    )
  }

  resolved <- candidates %>%
    anti_join(ambiguous, by = ".match_row_id") %>%
    distinct(.match_row_id, canonical_name, subgroup_id) %>%
    left_join(subgroup_uuid_lookup, by = c("canonical_name", "subgroup_id")) %>%
    select(.match_row_id, subgroup_entity_uuid = entity_uuid)

  df %>%
    left_join(resolved, by = ".match_row_id") %>%
    mutate(!!default_col := coalesce(subgroup_entity_uuid, .data[[default_col]])) %>%
    select(-.match_row_id, -subgroup_entity_uuid)
}
```

```{r}
# anyhing in names 2026 that's not in entity mapping?
```

```{r}
org_req_cols   <- c("to_add_status", "entity_name", "canonical_name", "review_group_id", "confirmed_link")
indiv_req_cols <- c("entity_name", "canonical_name", "entity_group_id", "confirmed_link")

# load feedback from review queues
load_feedback <- function(path, req_cols) {
  if (is.null(path) || !file.exists(path)) return(NULL)
  df <- read.csv(path, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
  if (nrow(df) == 0 || !all(req_cols %in% names(df))) return(NULL)
  out      <- df[, req_cols]
  out$flag              <- if ("flag"              %in% names(df)) df$flag              else NA_character_
  out$original_group_id <- if ("original_group_id" %in% names(df)) df$original_group_id else NA_character_ # original review groups as an indicator for what was compared
  out
}

# no-link registry: all confirmed pairs from reviews that reviewer determined should
# not be liked under the same registry
# for each reviewed group, any two names in DIFFERENT subgroups are a confirmed not-linked
# pair — this includes singletons vs. sub-entities AND pairs across different sub-entities
# Pairs are stored and used to suppress already-reviewed pairs from future review queues
if (file.exists(NO_LINK_REGISTRY_PATH)) {
  no_link_registry <- read.csv(NO_LINK_REGISTRY_PATH, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
} else {
  no_link_registry <- tibble(name_a = character(), name_b = character(),
                              entity_type = character(), reviewed_date = character())
}

# each file is processed independently — group IDs are only compared within the same review queue file
# original_group_id column (added to queue outputs going forward) identifies the pre-split
# group; falls back to stripping the reviewer-added suffix letter(s) for older files.
extract_no_link_pairs <- function(fb, group_id_col, entity_type_label) {
  empty <- tibble(name_a = character(), name_b = character(),
                  entity_type = character(), reviewed_date = character())
  if (is.null(fb) || nrow(fb) == 0) return(empty)
  grp <- fb %>%
    filter(tolower(trimws(coalesce(confirmed_link, ""))) != "uncertain") %>%
    mutate(
      raw_name    = toupper(entity_name),
      subgroup_id = .data[[group_id_col]], # subgroup ids reflect which name variants were determined to be linked
      orig_grp    = coalesce(original_group_id, sub("_[a-z]+$", "", .data[[group_id_col]])) # replace added suffixes to reconstruct original review group ids
    ) %>%
    distinct(raw_name, subgroup_id, orig_grp)
  left  <- grp %>% rename(name_a = raw_name, sg_a = subgroup_id)
  right <- grp %>% rename(name_b = raw_name, sg_b = subgroup_id)
  left %>%
    inner_join(right, by = "orig_grp", relationship = "many-to-many") %>%
    filter(sg_a != sg_b, name_a < name_b) %>% 
    transmute(name_a = name_a, name_b = name_b,
              entity_type = entity_type_label, reviewed_date = as.character(Sys.Date())) %>%
    distinct()
}

new_no_link_org_pairs <- bind_rows(lapply(NEW_ORG_FEEDBACK_FILES, function(f) { # apply to each feedback file individually. 
  extract_no_link_pairs(load_feedback(f, org_req_cols), "review_group_id", "org")
}))
new_no_link_indiv_pairs <- bind_rows(lapply(NEW_INDIV_FEEDBACK_FILES, function(f) {
  extract_no_link_pairs(load_feedback(f, indiv_req_cols), "entity_group_id", "indiv")
}))
new_no_link_pairs <- bind_rows(new_no_link_org_pairs, new_no_link_indiv_pairs)

pair_key <- function(df) paste(df$name_a, df$name_b, df$entity_type, sep = "|||") # key to distinguish pairs
no_link_registry <- bind_rows(
  new_no_link_pairs,
  no_link_registry %>% filter(!pair_key(.) %in% pair_key(new_no_link_pairs))
)

# build confirmed mapping rows from 2026 Names + entity registry
names_from_b <- names_2026 %>%

extra_from_c <- name_entity_mapping_existing %>% # anything not yet added to Names 2026 (typically, it should have been added already)
  filter(!((raw_name) %in% (names_from_b$raw_name)))

name_entity_mapping <- bind_rows(names_from_b, extra_from_c)

entity_registry <- name_entity_mapping %>%

# check for raw_name associated w/ multiple canonical names. 
# duplicate rows with the SAME canonical are harmless - will be collapsed below
raw_name_conflicts <- name_entity_mapping %>%
  filter(!is.na(canonical_name)) %>%
  group_by(raw_name) %>%
  summarise(n_canonical    = n_distinct(canonical_name),

if (nrow(raw_name_conflicts) > 0) {

  filter(!is.na(canonical_name), !is.na(entity_uuid)) %>%

            .groups = "drop") %>%

if (nrow(uuid_canonical_conflicts) > 0) {

                  nrow(uuid_canonical_conflicts)))

}

  distinct(raw_name, .keep_all = TRUE)

# in map, add rows where the raw_name = canonical_name so name variants can be compared against canonical names as well.

  filter(!is.na(canonical_name), confirmed == TRUE) %>%
  distinct(canonical_name, .keep_all = TRUE) %>%
  transmute(

    entity_uuid    = entity_uuid,
```

# ENTITY RESOLUTION / NAME VARIANT MATCHING

Apply name variant matching, fuzzy matching and custom record linkage algorithm to identify contributors that are likely the same, but associated with different name variants. 
Name variants will be manually reviewed and if confirmed, they will be added to the Names 2026 mapping. 
After all name variants are added to the map, contributors will then be aggregated by their `Normalized` name. 

## Organizations

1. Name variant linkage: name variants of an org name are compared for exact matches. Name variants include removing business ending, removing parentheses, etc.
2. Fuzzy matching performed on org name to id additional potential pairs.
3. DD org concept maps used to surface potential links between org names. 

```{r}
# make variants of each contributor name
make_name_variants <- function(df, col) {
  df %>% mutate(
    name_v1 = standardize_names(.data[[col]]) %>% fix_typos(), # simple standardization and known typos corrected
    name_v2 = remove_pac_info(name_v1)        %>% str_squish(), # removing FEC ID, FED PAC ID, MAJOR DONOR ID
    # remove name_v3 -> need to rename
    name_v4 = str_remove_all(name_v1, "\\s*\\(.*?\\)") %>% str_squish(), # remove parentheses
    name_v5 = replace_business_text(name_v4)   %>% str_squish() # remove business ending e.g. inc, corporation, etc. 
  )
}

# look for exact matches between name variants. 
find_exact_variant_pairs <- function(pool, variant_col) {
  candidates <- pool %>%
    filter(!is.na(.data[[variant_col]]), .data[[variant_col]] != "") %>%
    group_by(across(all_of(variant_col))) %>%
    filter(n() > 1) %>%
    ungroup()

  if (nrow(candidates) == 0)
    return(tibble(.x = integer(), .y = integer(), match_source = character()))

  candidates %>%
    group_by(across(all_of(variant_col))) %>%
    group_modify(~ as_tibble(t(combn(.x$row_id, 2)), .name_repair = ~ c(".x", ".y"))) %>%
    ungroup() %>%
    select(.x, .y) %>%
    mutate(match_source = paste0("exact_", variant_col))
}
```

```{r}
orgs <- contributions %>%
  filter(entity_type == "organization") %>%
  mutate(cont_row_id = row_id) %>%          # preserve row_id before overwriting
  mutate(has_contributor_id = !is.na(effective_Contributor.ID) & str_trim(as.character(effective_Contributor.ID)) != "") %>%
  make_name_variants("Contributor.Name") %>%
  filter(!is.na(name_v1), name_v1 != "") %>%
  mutate(row_id = row_number())
```


## No-link registry data checks (can skip)

Surface any entities added to the no-link registry that SHOULDN'T be
there. 

```{r}
if (nrow(no_link_registry) > 0) {

  # (1) No exact pairs (name_a == name_b)
  self_pairs <- no_link_registry %>% filter(name_a == name_b)
  if (nrow(self_pairs) > 0) {
    cat(sprintf("WARNING (1): %d self-pair(s) where name_a == name_b:\n", nrow(self_pairs)))
    print(self_pairs)
  } else cat("Check 1 passed: no self-pairs.\n")

  # (2) No shared name variants across a no-link pair
  registry_name_variants <- tibble(name = union(no_link_registry$name_a, no_link_registry$name_b)) %>%
    make_name_variants("name")

  get_variants <- function(nm) {
    registry_name_variants %>%
      filter(name == nm) %>%
      select(name_v1, name_v2, name_v4, name_v5) %>%
      unlist() %>% na.omit() %>% unique() %>% as.character()
  }

  variant_conflicts <- no_link_registry %>%
    rowwise() %>%
    mutate(
      .vars_a     = list(get_variants(name_a)),
      .vars_b     = list(get_variants(name_b)),
      .shared     = list(intersect(.vars_a, .vars_b)),
      .has_shared = length(.shared) > 0
    ) %>%
    filter(.has_shared) %>%
    mutate(shared_variants = paste(.shared, collapse = " | ")) %>%
    select(name_a, name_b, entity_type, shared_variants) %>%
    ungroup()

  if (nrow(variant_conflicts) > 0) {
    cat(sprintf("WARNING (2): %d no-link pair(s) share a name variant:\n", nrow(variant_conflicts)))
    print(variant_conflicts)
  } else cat("Check 2 passed: no shared name variants.\n")

  # (3) No shared Contributor.ID across a no-link pair (org pairs only)
  org_id_lookup <- orgs %>%
    filter(!is.na(effective_Contributor.ID),
           str_trim(as.character(effective_Contributor.ID)) != "") %>%
    mutate(.name_key = toupper(name_v1)) %>%
    select(.name_key, effective_Contributor.ID) %>%
    distinct()

  get_ids <- function(nm) {
    org_id_lookup %>%
      filter(.name_key == nm) %>%
      pull(effective_Contributor.ID) %>%
      as.character() %>% unique()
  }

  id_conflicts <- no_link_registry %>%
    filter(entity_type == "org") %>%
    rowwise() %>%
    mutate(
      .ids_a      = list(get_ids(name_a)),
      .ids_b      = list(get_ids(name_b)),
      .shared     = list(intersect(.ids_a, .ids_b)),
      .has_shared = length(.shared) > 0
    ) %>%
    filter(.has_shared) %>%
    mutate(shared_ids = paste(.shared, collapse = " | ")) %>%
    select(name_a, name_b, entity_type, shared_ids) %>%
    ungroup()

  if (nrow(id_conflicts) > 0) {
    cat(sprintf("WARNING (3): %d no-link pair(s) share a Contributor.ID:\n", nrow(id_conflicts)))
    print(id_conflicts)
  } else cat("Check 3 passed: no shared Contributor.IDs.\n")

  # (4) No shared chapter/unit numbers (digit sequences) across a no-link pair
  chapter_conflicts <- no_link_registry %>%
    rowwise() %>%
    mutate(
      .digits_a   = list(str_extract_all(name_a, "\\d+")[[1]]),
      .digits_b   = list(str_extract_all(name_b, "\\d+")[[1]]),
      .shared     = list(intersect(.digits_a, .digits_b)),
      .has_shared = length(.digits_a) > 0 & length(.digits_b) > 0 & length(.shared) > 0
    ) %>%
    filter(.has_shared) %>%
    mutate(shared_numbers = paste(.shared, collapse = " | ")) %>%
    select(name_a, name_b, entity_type, shared_numbers) %>%
    ungroup()

  if (nrow(chapter_conflicts) > 0) {
    cat(sprintf("NOTE (4): %d no-link pair(s) share digit sequences (check chapter numbers):\n",
                nrow(chapter_conflicts)))
    print(chapter_conflicts)
  } else cat("Check 4 passed: no shared chapter/unit numbers.\n")

} else {
  cat("No-link registry is empty — skipping checks.\n")
}
```

## Step 2: Exact variant cascade

```{r}
# look for exact matches between name variants. 
find_exact_variant_pairs <- function(pool, variant_col) {
  candidates <- pool %>%
    filter(!is.na(.data[[variant_col]]), .data[[variant_col]] != "") %>%
    group_by(across(all_of(variant_col))) %>%
    filter(n() > 1) %>% # more than one record shares an exact match of the name variant
    ungroup()

  if (nrow(candidates) == 0)
    return(tibble(.x = integer(), .y = integer(), match_source = character()))

  candidates %>%
    group_by(across(all_of(variant_col))) %>%
    group_modify(~ as_tibble(t(combn(.x$row_id, 2)), .name_repair = ~ c(".x", ".y"))) %>% # create pairs
    ungroup() %>%
    select(.x, .y) %>%
    mutate(match_source = paste0("exact_", variant_col))
}
```


```{r}
id_resolved_rows <- unique(c(id_auto_pairs$.x, id_auto_pairs$.y)) # contribution records already linked through contributor.id
#remaining_orgs   <- orgs %>% filter(!row_id %in% id_resolved_rows) # filter out records that were already grouped through a contributor.id match
remaining_orgs <- orgs # include ALL orgs so we can link PACs and non-PACs

variant_cols     <- c("name_v1", "name_v2", "name_v4", "name_v5") # skips name_v3 which removes unit info
seen_pairs       <- tibble(.x = integer(), .y = integer())
exact_pairs_list <- list()

for (v in variant_cols) {
  new_pairs <- find_exact_variant_pairs(orgs, v) %>%
    anti_join(seen_pairs, by = c(".x", ".y"))
  if (nrow(new_pairs) > 0) {
    exact_pairs_list[[v]] <- new_pairs
    seen_pairs <- bind_rows(seen_pairs, new_pairs %>% select(.x, .y))
  }
  cat("variant", v, "- new pairs:", nrow(new_pairs), "\n")
}

exact_pairs <- bind_rows(exact_pairs_list) %>%  # no dedup needed; each pair has its most-specific source
  left_join(orgs %>% select(row_id, id_x = effective_Contributor.ID, has_id_x = has_contributor_id), by = c(".x" = "row_id")) %>%
  left_join(orgs %>% select(row_id, id_y = effective_Contributor.ID, has_id_y = has_contributor_id), by = c(".y" = "row_id")) %>%
  mutate(link_tier = if_else(
    coalesce(has_id_x, FALSE) & coalesce(has_id_y, FALSE) & coalesce(id_x != id_y, FALSE),
    "review", "auto_link"
  )) %>%
  select(.x, .y, link_tier, match_source)

cat(sprintf("Exact cascade: %d auto-links, %d conflicting-ID review pairs\n",
            sum(exact_pairs$link_tier == "auto_link"),
            sum(exact_pairs$link_tier == "review")))

exact_pairs %>%
  filter(link_tier == "review") %>%
  left_join(orgs %>% select(row_id, name_x = Contributor.Name, id_x = effective_Contributor.ID), by = c(".x" = "row_id")) %>%
  left_join(orgs %>% select(row_id, name_y = Contributor.Name, id_y = effective_Contributor.ID), by = c(".y" = "row_id")) %>%
  select(name_x, id_x, name_y, id_y, match_source) %>%
  distinct() %>% print(n = 50)
```

```{r}
exact_pairs %>%
  filter(link_tier == "review") %>%
  left_join(orgs %>% select(row_id, name_x = Contributor.Name, id_x = effective_Contributor.ID), by = c(".x" = "row_id")) %>%
  left_join(orgs %>% select(row_id, name_y = Contributor.Name, id_y = effective_Contributor.ID), by = c(".y" = "row_id")) %>%
```

### Step 3: internal fuzzy match

The fuzzy match is the most expensive, so it doesn't run on all orgs like the other matching processes do.

1. Group orgs by links that were already estblished through contributor.id matches and name variant matches.
   The most common name per group is chosen as the `name_rep` for the group and used to fuzzy match against.
   The goal is to identify other possible name variants belonging to already-established groups that weren't
   already found during the id alias and name variant step.
2. Perform fuzzy matching on all unresolved org names + the name reps from each org group.
   This step keeps constraint that conflicting-id matches are paired since fuzzy matching is much looser, 
   but could consider removing this constraint. 

```{r}
# id and exact pairs to get one rep per already-established cluster
all_early_pairs <- bind_rows(
  id_auto_pairs %>% select(.x, .y),
  exact_pairs   %>% filter(link_tier == "auto_link") %>% select(.x, .y) # doesn't include contributor.id conflicts
)

if (nrow(all_early_pairs) > 0) {
  g_early       <- graph_from_data_frame(all_early_pairs, directed = FALSE,
                                          vertices = data.frame(name = orgs$row_id))
  early_members <- components(g_early)$membership
  cluster_reps  <- tibble(row_id = as.integer(names(early_members)), cluster = early_members) %>%
    left_join(orgs %>% select(row_id, name_v5), by = "row_id") %>%
    add_count(cluster, name_v5, name = "n_v5") %>%
    group_by(cluster) %>%
    slice_max(n_v5, n = 1, with_ties = TRUE) %>%   # most common name_v5 in cluster
    slice_min(row_id, n = 1, with_ties = FALSE) %>% # tiebreak: lowest row_id
    pull(row_id)
} else {
  cluster_reps <- integer(0)
}

linked_row_ids <- unique(c(all_early_pairs$.x, all_early_pairs$.y))

# name_reps: one rep per name_v5, covering:
#   - cluster reps (most-common name_v5 per linked group — represents whole cluster for fuzzy)
#   - unlinked singletons (not in any early pair)
name_reps <- orgs %>%
  filter(row_id %in% cluster_reps | !row_id %in% linked_row_ids) %>%
  group_by(name_v5) %>% 
  slice_min(row_id, n = 1, with_ties = FALSE) %>% # those with more than one name_v5, not already-linked are those with diff ids i think 
  ungroup()

cat(sprintf("Fuzzy matching input: %d name reps\n", nrow(name_reps)))
```


```{r}
# token Jaccard: exact token-overlap ratio between two name strings
token_jaccard <- function(a, b) {
  tok_a <- str_split(str_squish(a), "\\s+")[[1]]
  tok_b <- str_split(str_squish(b), "\\s+")[[1]]
  n_int <- length(intersect(tok_a, tok_b))
  n_uni <- length(union(tok_a, tok_b))
  if (n_uni == 0) return(0)
  n_int / n_uni
}

cat(sprintf("name_reps: %d rows\n", nrow(name_reps)))

# add chunks to help with memory issues
# candidate pairs via stringdist_inner_join 
# chunks splits the left side into batches of CHUNK_SIZE
# each batch joins against the full right side, so every
# pair is evaluated exactly once (when the lower row_id is on the left).
CHUNK_SIZE <- 500L
name_reps_right <- name_reps %>%
  rename(row_id_y = row_id, name_v5_y = name_v5) %>%
  select(row_id_y, name_v5_y)

chunks <- split(
  name_reps %>% select(row_id, name_v5),
  ceiling(seq_len(nrow(name_reps)) / CHUNK_SIZE)
)

fuzzy_candidates <- bind_rows(lapply(chunks, function(chunk) {
  stringdist_inner_join(
    chunk,
    name_reps_right,
    by           = c("name_v5" = "name_v5_y"),
    method       = "jw", p = 0.1, max_dist = 0.12,
    distance_col = "jw_dist"
  ) %>%
    filter(row_id < row_id_y)
})) %>%
  rename(.x = row_id, .y = row_id_y, name_x = name_v5, name_y = name_v5_y)

rm(chunks, name_reps_right)
gc(verbose = FALSE)

cat(sprintf("Fuzzy candidates (JW dist <= 0.12): %d pairs (from %d reps)\n",
            nrow(fuzzy_candidates), nrow(name_reps)))

# score all candidate pairs and flag conflicting-ID pairs before splitting
org_pairs_scored <- fuzzy_candidates %>%
  left_join(orgs %>% select(row_id, id_x = effective_Contributor.ID, has_id_x = has_contributor_id),
            by = c(".x" = "row_id")) %>%
  left_join(orgs %>% select(row_id, id_y = effective_Contributor.ID, has_id_y = has_contributor_id),
            by = c(".y" = "row_id")) %>%
  mutate(
    has_id_conflict = coalesce(has_id_x, FALSE) & coalesce(has_id_y, FALSE) & coalesce(id_x != id_y, FALSE),
    jaccard     = mapply(token_jaccard, name_x, name_y),
    name_jw     = 1 - jw_dist,
    name_cosine = bigram_cosine(name_x, name_y)
  ) %>%
  filter(jaccard >= 0.40) %>%   # more lenient threshold 
  mutate(
    name_sim  = (name_jw + name_cosine) / 2,
    link_tier = case_when(
      name_jw  >= 0.999 ~ "auto_link",
      name_sim >= 0.90  ~ "auto_link",
      name_sim >= 0.85  ~ "review",
      TRUE              ~ "no_link"
    ),
    match_source = "internal_fuzzy"
  )

# conflicting-ID pairs that pass scoring thresholds (currently excluded from org_pairs)
#cat("\nFuzzy pairs with conflicting contributor IDs that would be linked:\n")
conflicting_id_links <- org_pairs_scored %>%
  filter(has_id_conflict, link_tier != "no_link") %>%
  left_join(orgs %>% select(row_id, Contributor.Name), by = c(".x" = "row_id")) %>%
  left_join(orgs %>% select(row_id, Contributor.Name), by = c(".y" = "row_id"), suffix = c("_x", "_y")) %>%
  select(Contributor.Name_x, id_x, Contributor.Name_y, id_y, name_sim, link_tier) 

# org_pairs: conflicting IDs still excluded
org_pairs <- org_pairs_scored %>%
  filter(!has_id_conflict) %>%
  select(.x, .y, id_x, id_y, has_id_x, has_id_y, name_x, name_y,
         jaccard, name_sim, name_jw, name_cosine, link_tier, match_source)

# flag different-chapter pairs: names identical after stripping digits AND the name
# contains a chapter indicator 
CHAPTER_RE <- regex("\\b(LOCAL|LODGE|CHAPTER|COUNCIL|DISTRICT|UNIT|UNION|MEMBER DUES)\\b|\\b[A-Za-z]{2,4}\\s+\\d{3,4}\\b", ignore_case = TRUE)

org_pairs <- org_pairs %>%
  mutate(
    nx_no_digits = str_remove_all(name_x, "\\d+") %>% str_squish(),
    ny_no_digits = str_remove_all(name_y, "\\d+") %>% str_squish(),
    diff_chapter = str_detect(name_x, "\\d") & str_detect(name_y, "\\d") &
                   nx_no_digits == ny_no_digits &
                   (str_detect(name_x, CHAPTER_RE) | str_detect(name_y, CHAPTER_RE))
  ) %>%
  select(-nx_no_digits, -ny_no_digits)

# review before removing — check that nothing legitimate is being caught
diff_chapter_pairs <- org_pairs %>%
  filter(diff_chapter, link_tier != "no_link") %>%
  left_join(orgs %>% select(row_id, Contributor.Name), by = c(".x" = "row_id")) %>%
  left_join(orgs %>% select(row_id, Contributor.Name), by = c(".y" = "row_id"), suffix = c("_x", "_y")) %>%
  select(Contributor.Name_x, Contributor.Name_y, name_sim, link_tier) 

org_pairs <- org_pairs %>%
  filter(!diff_chapter) %>%
  select(-diff_chapter)

cat(sprintf("\nFuzzy: %d auto-links, %d review pairs, %d no-link (Jaccard >= 0.40)\n",
            sum(org_pairs$link_tier == "auto_link"),
            sum(org_pairs$link_tier == "review"),
            sum(org_pairs$link_tier == "no_link")))
```

## Step 5: External bridge map

Use Digital Democracy's org concept mapping to surface additional links. 
This helps identify organizations with very different names that may not 
be caught by fuzzy matching. 

DD org concepts are looser than our links (e.g. all chapters of a union are linked under one 
org concept), so we don't want to automatically treat these as links.

This originally also used the equivalent of Names 2026 as a bridge; but that's no longer needed
since we are now using that directly in the entity resolution process. 

```{r}
# standardize external names to name_v5 format for matching
build_bridge_lookup <- function(mapping) {
  mapping %>%
    mutate(name_std = standardize_names(record_name) %>%
             fix_typos() %>%
             #remove_pac_info() %>%
             #remove_unit_info() %>%
             replace_business_text() %>%
             str_remove_all("\\s*\\(.*?\\)") %>%
             str_squish()) %>%
    select(name_std, canonical_name) %>%
    filter(!is.na(name_std), name_std != "", !is.na(canonical_name), canonical_name != "")
}

map1_lookup <- build_bridge_lookup(map1)

find_bridge_pairs <- function(orgs_df, lookup, source_label) {
  matched <- orgs_df %>%
    inner_join(lookup, by = c("name_v5" = "name_std")) %>%
    select(row_id, name_v5, canonical_name) %>%
    distinct(name_v5, canonical_name, .keep_all = TRUE) 

  if (nrow(matched) < 2) return(tibble(.x = integer(), .y = integer(),
                                        match_source = character(), canonical_name = character()))

  matched %>%
    rename(.x = row_id, name_v5_x = name_v5) %>%
    inner_join(matched %>% rename(.y = row_id, name_v5_y = name_v5), by = "canonical_name") %>%
    filter(.x < .y, name_v5_x != name_v5_y) %>%
    group_by(.x, .y) %>%
    mutate(
      n_canonicals = n_distinct(canonical_name),
      needs_review = n_canonicals > 1
    ) %>%
    ungroup() %>%
    mutate(match_source = source_label) %>%
    select(.x, .y, match_source, canonical_name, n_canonicals, needs_review)
}

```

```{r}
# appply bridge map to ALL orgs
bridge_map1 <- find_bridge_pairs(orgs, map1_lookup, "map1_bridge")
cat("Bridge pairs — map1:", nrow(bridge_map1), "\n")

bridge_map1 %>%
  mutate(.x = pmin(.x, .y), .y = pmax(.x, .y)) %>%
  distinct(.x, .y, canonical_name, .keep_all = TRUE) %>%
  left_join(orgs %>% select(row_id, name_x = Contributor.Name), by = c(".x" = "row_id")) %>%
  left_join(orgs %>% select(row_id, name_y = Contributor.Name), by = c(".y" = "row_id")) %>%
  select(name_x, name_y, canonical_name, n_canonicals) %>%
  arrange(name_x, name_y)
```


### combine bridge pairs

Note: upgrading fuzzy matches can be removed; this is mostly an artifact of 
the old entity-resolution process.

```{r}
# bridge pairs from map1 only
bridge_pairs <- bridge_map1 %>%
  group_by(.x, .y) %>%
  summarise(
    match_source   = paste(sort(unique(match_source)), collapse = "+"),
    canonical_name = paste(sort(unique(canonical_name)), collapse = " / "),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

# canonical ID per name_v5: if ANY contribution row for that name has an ID, record it
# used detect conflicting-ID pairs regardless of which row_id find_bridge_pairs picked.
# there are cases where name_v5 could have multiple contributor.ids
org_name_canonical_id <- orgs %>%
  filter(has_contributor_id) %>%
  group_by(name_v5) %>%
  summarise(canonical_id = names(sort(table(effective_Contributor.ID), decreasing = TRUE))[1],
            .groups = "drop")

# score bridge pairs on internal similarity
bridge_scored <- bridge_pairs %>%
  left_join(orgs %>% select(row_id, name_x = name_v5),
            by = c(".x" = "row_id")) %>%
  left_join(orgs %>% select(row_id, name_y = name_v5),
            by = c(".y" = "row_id")) %>%
  # join on name, not row_id in case a row was picked that didn't have a contributor.id
  left_join(org_name_canonical_id %>% rename(name_x = name_v5, id_x = canonical_id), by = "name_x") %>%
  left_join(org_name_canonical_id %>% rename(name_y = name_v5, id_y = canonical_id), by = "name_y") %>%
  mutate(
    has_id_conflict = coalesce(!is.na(id_x), FALSE) & coalesce(!is.na(id_y), FALSE) & coalesce(id_x != id_y, FALSE)
  )

# show conflicting-ID bridge pairs before filtering them out
#cat("\nBridge pairs with conflicting contributor IDs (currently excluded):\n")
# maybe change this so i can look at which are filtered out AFTER local units conflicts removed
bridge_id_conflicts <- bridge_scored %>%
  filter(has_id_conflict) %>%
  left_join(orgs %>% select(row_id, raw_name_x = Contributor.Name), by = c(".x" = "row_id")) %>%
  left_join(orgs %>% select(row_id, raw_name_y = Contributor.Name), by = c(".y" = "row_id")) %>%
  select(raw_name_x, id_x, raw_name_y, id_y, canonical_name) %>%
  arrange(canonical_name) 

bridge_scored <- bridge_scored %>%
  filter(!has_id_conflict) %>% # filters out id-conflicts
  mutate(
    name_jw     = stringsim(name_x, name_y, method = "jw", p = 0.1),
    name_cosine = bigram_cosine(name_x, name_y),
    name_sim    = (name_jw + name_cosine) / 2
  ) %>%
  select(-name_x, -name_y, -id_x, -id_y, -has_id_conflict)

# tag internal fuzzy paris thr bridge found— for match_source logging
internal_pair_keys <- org_pairs %>%
  filter(link_tier != "no_link") %>%
  mutate(pair_key = paste(pmin(.x, .y), pmax(.x, .y)))

bridge_pair_keys <- bridge_scored %>%
  mutate(pair_key = paste(pmin(.x, .y), pmax(.x, .y))) %>%
  select(pair_key, bridge_source = match_source)

# upgrade internal pairs corroborated by a bridge
BRIDGE_UPGRADE_THRESHOLD <- 0.65

org_pairs <- org_pairs %>%
  mutate(pair_key = paste(pmin(.x, .y), pmax(.x, .y))) %>%
  left_join(bridge_pair_keys, by = "pair_key") %>%
  mutate(
    match_source = if_else(!is.na(bridge_source),
                           paste(match_source, bridge_source, sep = "+"),
                           match_source),
    link_tier = case_when(
      link_tier == "review" & !is.na(bridge_source) & name_sim >= BRIDGE_UPGRADE_THRESHOLD ~ "auto_link",
      TRUE ~ link_tier
    )
  ) %>%
  select(-pair_key, -bridge_source)

# bridge-only pairs
bridge_only <- bridge_scored %>%
  mutate(pair_key = paste(pmin(.x, .y), pmax(.x, .y))) %>%
  filter(!pair_key %in% internal_pair_keys$pair_key) %>%
  select(-pair_key) %>%
  mutate(link_tier = "review")  # bridge alone never auto-links

# flag different-chapter pairs in bridge (same logic as fuzzy, with CHAPTER_RE guard)
#CHAPTER_RE <- "\\b(LOCAL|LODGE|CHAPTER|COUNCIL|DISTRICT|UNIT)\\b|^[A-Z]{2,5}\\s+\\d"
CHAPTER_RE <- regex("\\b(LOCAL|LODGE|CHAPTER|COUNCIL|DISTRICT|UNIT|UNION|MEMBER DUES)\\b|\\b[A-Za-z]{2,4}\\s+\\d{3,4}\\b", ignore_case = TRUE)

bridge_only <- bridge_only %>%
  left_join(orgs %>% select(row_id, name_x = name_v5), by = c(".x" = "row_id")) %>%
  left_join(orgs %>% select(row_id, name_y = name_v5), by = c(".y" = "row_id")) %>%
  mutate(
    nx_no_digits = str_remove_all(name_x, "\\d+") %>% str_squish(),
    ny_no_digits = str_remove_all(name_y, "\\d+") %>% str_squish(),
    diff_chapter = str_detect(name_x, "\\d") & str_detect(name_y, "\\d") &
                   nx_no_digits == ny_no_digits &
                   (str_detect(name_x, CHAPTER_RE) | str_detect(name_y, CHAPTER_RE))
  )

#cat("\nDifferent-chapter pairs flagged for removal (bridge):\n")
diff_chapter_bridge <- bridge_only %>%
  filter(diff_chapter) %>%
  left_join(orgs %>% select(row_id, Contributor.Name), by = c(".x" = "row_id")) %>%
  left_join(orgs %>% select(row_id, Contributor.Name), by = c(".y" = "row_id"), suffix = c("_x", "_y")) %>%
  select(Contributor.Name_x, Contributor.Name_y, canonical_name) 

bridge_only <- bridge_only %>%
  filter(!diff_chapter) %>%
  select(-name_x, -name_y, -nx_no_digits, -ny_no_digits, -diff_chapter)

cat("Bridge-corroborated internal pairs:", sum(!is.na(bridge_pair_keys$bridge_source[match(internal_pair_keys$pair_key, bridge_pair_keys$pair_key)])), "\n")
cat("Bridge-only new pairs for review:", nrow(bridge_only), "\n")
```

## Combine + cluster - definitive links

```{r}
# pairs joined through definitive links (not fuzzy matchin)
all_org_pairs <- bind_rows(
  id_auto_pairs %>% select(.x, .y, link_tier, match_source),
  exact_pairs,
)

# build one graph from all non-rejected pairs, treating review links as true
linkable_pairs <- all_org_pairs %>% filter(link_tier %in% c("auto_link", "review")) 

if (nrow(linkable_pairs) > 0) {
  g_orgs       <- graph_from_data_frame(linkable_pairs %>% select(.x, .y), directed = FALSE)
  org_clusters <- components(g_orgs)$membership

  org_cluster_raw <- tibble(row_id = as.integer(names(org_clusters)), cluster_num = org_clusters) %>%
    left_join(orgs %>% select(row_id, Contributor.Name, Contributor.ID, name_v5), by = "row_id")

  cluster_uuid_map <- org_cluster_raw %>%
    group_by(cluster_num) %>%
    summarise(raw_names = list(unique(Contributor.Name)), .groups = "drop") %>%
    rowwise() %>%
    mutate(
      result      = list(lookup_cluster_uuid(raw_names, nem_lookup)),
      entity_id   = result$entity_id,
      is_conflict = result$is_conflict,
      is_new      = result$is_new
    ) %>%
    ungroup() %>%
    select(cluster_num, entity_id, is_conflict, is_new)

  org_cluster_map <- org_cluster_raw %>%
    left_join(cluster_uuid_map, by = "cluster_num") %>%
    select(row_id, entity_id, is_conflict, is_new)
} else {
  org_cluster_map <- tibble(row_id = integer(), entity_id = character(),
                             is_conflict = logical(), is_new = logical())
}

orgs_singleton_lookup <- orgs %>%
  filter(!row_id %in% org_cluster_map$row_id) %>%
  distinct(Contributor.Name) %>%
  mutate(raw_name_key = toupper(Contributor.Name)) %>%
  left_join(nem_lookup %>% select(raw_name, entity_uuid), by = c("raw_name_key" = "raw_name")) %>%
  mutate(
    is_new    = is.na(entity_uuid),
    entity_id = coalesce(entity_uuid, UUIDgenerate(n = n()))
  ) %>%
  select(Contributor.Name, entity_id, is_new)

orgs_singletons <- orgs %>%
  filter(!row_id %in% org_cluster_map$row_id) %>%
  left_join(orgs_singleton_lookup, by = "Contributor.Name") %>%
  mutate(is_conflict = FALSE) %>%
  select(row_id, entity_id, is_new, is_conflict)

orgs_resolved <- orgs %>%
  left_join(bind_rows(org_cluster_map, orgs_singletons), by = "row_id")

```


## Org name variant review queue

For each entity with more than one distinct name, output the names that are not already
tracked so they can be added to the name variant list. `entity_status` indicates whether
this is a new name variant of a known entity or a new entity group entirely. 

```{r}
# grouping for name variant review queue: includes fuzzy + bridge in addition to id and exact
all_org_pairs_review <- bind_rows(
  id_auto_pairs %>% select(.x, .y, link_tier, match_source),
  exact_pairs   %>% select(.x, .y, link_tier, match_source),
  org_pairs     %>% filter(link_tier != "no_link") %>% select(.x, .y, link_tier, match_source),
  bridge_only   %>% select(.x, .y, link_tier, match_source)
)

# drop pairs where both names are confirmed as DIFFERENT entities in name_entity_mapping
# uses nem_lookup so UUIDs are stable; names w/out a canonical name stay NA 
# the all_confirmed mechanism handles those groups separately
confirmed_nem <- nem_lookup %>% filter(confirmed == TRUE) %>% select(raw_name, entity_uuid) # all of these should have confirmed = TRUE, but just in case
orgs_known_uuid <- orgs %>%
  transmute(row_id,
            known_uuid = confirmed_nem$entity_uuid[match(toupper(Contributor.Name), confirmed_nem$raw_name)])

n_before_split_filter <- nrow(all_org_pairs_review)
# remove pairs that matched to different uuids (if name is already in map, it means it was verified manually)
all_org_pairs_review <- all_org_pairs_review %>%
  left_join(orgs_known_uuid %>% rename(uuid_x = known_uuid), by = c(".x" = "row_id")) %>%
  left_join(orgs_known_uuid %>% rename(uuid_y = known_uuid), by = c(".y" = "row_id")) %>%
  filter(is.na(uuid_x) | is.na(uuid_y) | uuid_x == uuid_y) %>% # only include pairs where at least one uuid is known OR they have the same uuid 
  select(.x, .y, link_tier, match_source)
cat(sprintf("Split-entity filter: removed %d pairs where both names had confirmed different UUIDs\n",
            n_before_split_filter - nrow(all_org_pairs_review)))

# create graph now that false matches are removed
if (nrow(all_org_pairs_review) > 0) {
  g_org_review     <- graph_from_data_frame(all_org_pairs_review %>% select(.x, .y), directed = FALSE)
  org_review_comps <- components(g_org_review)$membership
  org_review_group_map <- tibble(
    row_id          = as.integer(names(org_review_comps)),
    review_group_id = paste0("org_rg_", org_review_comps)
  )
} else {
  org_review_group_map <- tibble(row_id = integer(), review_group_id = character())
}

# pair filter above removes direct edges between confirmed-different-entity
# names, but transitive paths through unconfirmed names can still group different entities together
# for any component that contains multiple distinct confirmed UUIDs, re-assign confirmed names to
# UUID-based subgroups - unconfirmed names keep the original review_group_id and remain in the queue
orgs_confirmed_uuid <- orgs %>%
  transmute(row_id, raw_name = toupper(Contributor.Name)) %>%
  left_join(confirmed_nem, by = "raw_name") %>%
  select(row_id, confirmed_uuid = entity_uuid)

org_review_group_map <- org_review_group_map %>%
  left_join(orgs_confirmed_uuid, by = "row_id") %>%
  group_by(review_group_id) %>%
  mutate(n_distinct_uuid = n_distinct(confirmed_uuid[!is.na(confirmed_uuid)])) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  mutate(
    review_group_id = case_when(
      n_distinct_uuid > 1 & !is.na(confirmed_uuid) ~ paste0("org_rg_confirmed_", confirmed_uuid),
      TRUE                                           ~ review_group_id 
    )
  ) %>%
  select(row_id, review_group_id)

cat(sprintf("Post-hoc UUID split: %d groups contain confirmed names re-assigned to UUID-based subgroups\n",
            sum(grepl("^org_rg_confirmed_", org_review_group_map$review_group_id))))

# flag review groups that contain names with conflicting non-NA Contributor.IDs (just a flag for reference in review queue)
org_cid <- orgs %>%
  select(row_id, cid = effective_Contributor.ID) %>%
  mutate(cid = na_if(str_trim(as.character(cid)), ""))

conflicting_rg <- org_review_group_map %>%
  left_join(org_cid, by = "row_id") %>%
  filter(!is.na(cid)) %>%
  group_by(review_group_id) %>%
  filter(n_distinct(cid) > 1) %>%
  pull(review_group_id) %>%
  unique()

org_review_singletons <- orgs %>%
  filter(!row_id %in% org_review_group_map$row_id) %>%
  transmute(row_id, review_group_id = paste0("org_rg_solo_", row_id))

org_review_groups <- bind_rows(org_review_group_map, org_review_singletons)

```

why many-to-many for join in paired_qualifying? 

```{r}
# map review_group_id -> all raw contributor names in that group; expands beyond the
# single representative row_id chosen during fuzzy/bridge matching so that all
# contribution rows for each name are included in the $5k threshold check.
org_group_name_index <- org_review_group_map %>%
  left_join(
    orgs %>%
      mutate(raw_name_key = str_squish(toupper(Contributor.Name))) %>%
      select(row_id, raw_name_key),
    by = "row_id"
  ) %>%
  distinct(review_group_id, raw_name_key) # all names associated w/ each review group 

# paired groups: expand ALL contribution rows for names in the group via raw name
paired_qualifying <- orgs %>%
  mutate(
    raw_name_key = str_squish(toupper(Contributor.Name)),
    rc_id        = as.character(Recipient.Committee.ID)
  ) %>%
  inner_join(org_group_name_index, by = "raw_name_key", relationship = "many-to-one") %>%
  filter(rc_id %in% relevant_recipient_ids)

# singletons: orgs not in any paired group, kept under their own solo review_group_id
solo_qualifying <- orgs %>%
  mutate(
    raw_name_key = str_squish(toupper(Contributor.Name)),
    rc_id        = as.character(Recipient.Committee.ID)
  ) %>%
  filter(!raw_name_key %in% org_group_name_index$raw_name_key) %>%
  left_join(org_review_singletons %>% select(row_id, review_group_id), by = "row_id") %>%
  filter(rc_id %in% relevant_recipient_ids)

qualifying_expanded <- bind_rows(paired_qualifying, solo_qualifying)

qualifying_review_groups <- qualifying_expanded %>%
  mutate(
    race_recipient_key = case_when(
      coalesce(is_pac_contribution, FALSE)          ~ rc_id,
      !is.na(Ballot.Measure) & Ballot.Measure != "" ~ Ballot.Measure,
      !is.na(Office) & Office != ""                 ~ paste(Recipient.Name, Office, sep = " | "),
      TRUE                                          ~ Recipient.Name
    )
  ) %>%
  group_by(review_group_id, race_recipient_key) %>%
  summarise(total = sum(Amount, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") %>%

qualifying_pac_filer_ids <- qualifying_expanded %>%
```

# INDIVIDUALS:

Entity resolution for individuals.Entity resolution (in the context of categorizations) is used to 
determine who meets the $5k threshold to be categorized. For mapping name variants, we want to surface name variants WITHIN
recipient committees, since aggregation won't happen across recipient committees.

Process: 
1. Filter the individuals data to only include contributors to PACs that meet the $5k threshold. 
2. Parse names into first, last and if applicable, middle, prefix and suffix
3. Build record linkage algorithm that scores how similar individuals are based on their name,
   employer, occupation, city, etc. 
4. Create name variant review queue for individuals - contributors that are likely the same person,
   but contributed under slightly different names.
5. Create a "disambiguation" review queue that flags contributors with the exact same name (meaning
   they would normally be aggregated) who were flagged as different people by the record linkage
   algorithm.
