### record linkage algorithm

Block on Recipient.Committee.ID so we only compare pairs within recipient committees.
Pairs are compared if:
- they have the same last_meta and zip code (within the same recipient committee)
- they have the same last_meta and first initial (within the same recipient committee)

Note: 
- Doing this record linkage algorithm across the entire dataset was too expensive 
- Limitation is that this will limit our ability to link name variants of individuals across committees
  to make sure they are being categorized consistently. But won't be an issue for contributions that used
  the exact same name across contributions to different committees. 

Threshold logic: 
- Pairs are not linked if the first names are too different: this was added because many linked pairs were husband/wife
or family members where the two people had the same last name, same city/zip, and first name that started with
the same letter (but were clearly different people).
- A stricter threshold is used for people with names that are more common in the data. e.g. Michael Brown should
only be linked to another Michael Brown if info is very similar. Lower threshold used for people with less common names. 
- A stricter threshold is also used for pairs where the employer/occupation are uninformative. E.g. so many people have
'retired' or 'not employed' as their employer, which is not very strong evidence to link people. 

Thresholds were adjusted and additional requirements were added after doing several rounds of review of linked pairs.
The original goal was to have stricter matching requirements in order to err on the side of not linking contributors
if there was uncertainty, but this means it may not link people like Bill Bloomfield who has very little info that
ties his records together apart from his name (uninformative employer/occupation, different zip codes across contributions).

### Scoring function summary

Each candidate pair is scored using a weighted combination of similarities between their fields, 
normalized by the sum of active weights so the scale is preserved when fields drop out:

| Field | Comparator | Base weight |
|---|---|---|
| Last name | Jaro-Winkler | 0.30 |
| First name | Jaro-Winkler | 0.25 |
| Employer | Cosine bigram similarity | 0.25 (drops to 0 if both sides uninformative) |
| Occupation | Exact match | 0.10 (drops to 0 if both sides uninformative) |
| Zip code | Exact match | 0.07 |
| City | Jaro-Winkler | 0.03 |

**Uninformative values**: blank, NA, UNKNOWN, RETIRED, NONE, SELF EMPLOYED. 
When one side of a pair has an uninformative employer/occupation and the other does not, the similarity for that field is set to 0 (penalizing the pair for asymmetry). 
When both sides are uninformative, the field weight drops to 0 and the field is excluded from scoring entirely. 
`any_context_dropped` is TRUE when either field (employer or occupation) is excluded — this triggers a stricter match threshold.

**Threshold tiers** (applied after scoring):

| Condition | Threshold |
|---|---|
| Common name + any context dropped | `COMMON_NAME_STRICT` (0.97) |
| Common name | `COMMON_NAME_THRESHOLD` (0.93) |
| Any context dropped | `STRICT_THRESHOLD` (0.94) |
| Default | `MATCH_THRESHOLD` (0.90) |

Common name = last name appears ≥ 3 times AND first name appears ≥ 3 times in the data. 
Pairs are always `no_link` if first name similarity < 0.85, or if there is a city conflict combined with any dropped context field.

```{r}
# Constants
UNINFORMATIVE_VALS        <- c("UNKNOWN", "RETIRED", "NONE", "SELF EMPLOYED") # uninformative values of employer/occupation (after these variables are processed to standardize N/A types of values)
FIRST_NAME_MIN            <- 0.85 
MATCH_THRESHOLD           <- 0.90
STRICT_THRESHOLD          <- 0.94  # both employer & occupation uninformative
COMMON_NAME_THRESHOLD     <- 0.93  # common name, employer informative
COMMON_NAME_STRICT        <- 0.97  # common name + both uninformative
UNCERTAIN_LOW             <- 0.75
EMPLOYER_CONFLICT_SIM     <- 0.70  # employer similarity below this = conflict
RARE_NAME_UNCERTAIN_LOW <- 0.65 
COMMON_LAST_MIN           <- 3
COMMON_FIRST_MIN          <- 3
RARE_NAME_UNCERTAIN_LOW   <- 0.65
```

```{r}
# scoring function
compare_and_score_indiv <- function(pairs_obj, df) {
  if (nrow(pairs_obj) == 0) return(tibble())
  pairs_obj %>%
    compare_pairs(
      on = c("last_name", "first_name", "zip_code_processed",
             "processed_employer_name", "processed_occupation", "standardized_city"),
      default_comparator = cmp_jarowinkler(),
      comparators = list(
        processed_employer_name = function(a, b) stringsim(a, b, method = "cosine", q = 2),
        zip_code_processed      = cmp_identical(),
        processed_occupation    = cmp_identical()
      )
    ) %>%
    as_tibble() %>%
    
    # join raw employer/occupation values
    left_join(df %>% select(row_id, emp_a = processed_employer_name, occ_a = processed_occupation,
                             city_a = standardized_city),
              by = c(".x" = "row_id")) %>%
    left_join(df %>% select(row_id, emp_b = processed_employer_name, occ_b = processed_occupation,
                             city_b = standardized_city),
              by = c(".y" = "row_id")) %>%
    mutate(
      emp_a_uninf = emp_a %in% UNINFORMATIVE_VALS | is.na(emp_a) | emp_a == "",
      emp_b_uninf = emp_b %in% UNINFORMATIVE_VALS | is.na(emp_b) | emp_b == "",
      occ_a_uninf = occ_a %in% UNINFORMATIVE_VALS | is.na(occ_a) | occ_a == "",
      occ_b_uninf = occ_b %in% UNINFORMATIVE_VALS | is.na(occ_b) | occ_b == "",
      
      w_emp  = if_else(emp_a_uninf & emp_b_uninf, 0,    0.25),
      w_occ  = if_else(occ_a_uninf & occ_b_uninf, 0,    0.10),
      w_tot  = 0.30 + 0.25 + w_emp + w_occ + 0.07 + 0.03,
      emp_sim = if_else(emp_a_uninf | emp_b_uninf, 0, coalesce(processed_employer_name, 0)),
      occ_sim = if_else(occ_a_uninf | occ_b_uninf, 0, coalesce(processed_occupation, 0)),
      score  = (0.30 * coalesce(last_name, 0) +
                0.25 * coalesce(first_name, 0) +
                w_emp * emp_sim +
                w_occ * occ_sim +
                0.07 * coalesce(zip_code_processed, 0) +
                0.03 * coalesce(standardized_city, 0)) / w_tot,
      
      # flag cases where employer and occupation are uninformative (e.g. not employed)
      # don't want uninformative values to increase similarity between pairs
      both_uninformative  = (emp_a_uninf & emp_b_uninf) & (occ_a_uninf & occ_b_uninf),
      # TRUE when either contextual field drops from scoring (both emp uninf OR both occ uninf)
      any_context_dropped = (emp_a_uninf & emp_b_uninf) | (occ_a_uninf & occ_b_uninf),
    
      
      # flag cases where one employer is the substring of the other employer in the pair 
      employer_substring = !emp_a_uninf & !emp_b_uninf & mapply(
        function(a, b) {
          if (is.na(a) || is.na(b) || a == "" || b == "") return(FALSE)
          a <- toupper(a); b <- toupper(b)
          grepl(b, a, fixed = TRUE) || grepl(a, b, fixed = TRUE)
        },
        emp_a, emp_b,
        USE.NAMES = FALSE
      ),
    
      employer_conflict  = !emp_a_uninf & !emp_b_uninf &
                           !employer_substring &
                           coalesce(processed_employer_name, 0) < EMPLOYER_CONFLICT_SIM,
    
      # city conflict: both cities are known and different (JW < 0.85)
      city_conflict = (!is.na(city_a) & city_a != "") &
                      (!is.na(city_b) & city_b != "") &
                      coalesce(standardized_city, 1) < 0.85
    ) %>%
    select(-occ_a, -occ_b,
           -emp_a_uninf, -emp_b_uninf, -occ_a_uninf, -occ_b_uninf,
           -w_emp, -w_occ, -w_tot, -emp_sim, -occ_sim,
           -city_a, -city_b)
}
```

### blocking and scoring

```{r}
# pair_blocking by Recipient.Committee.ID × last_meta

INDIV_PAIRS_TMP <- "08_outputs/indiv_pairs_tmp.csv"
if (file.exists(INDIV_PAIRS_TMP)) file.remove(INDIV_PAIRS_TMP)
first_written <- FALSE

# split into a named list of dataframes — one per (committee × last_meta) group.
indiv_filtered <- individuals %>%
  filter(!is.na(last_meta), last_meta != "", !is.na(Recipient.Committee.ID))

# for hyphenated last names (e.g. "SMITH-JONES"), add extra rows with each component's
# metaphone
hyphen_rows <- indiv_filtered %>%
  filter(str_detect(coalesce(last_name, ""), "-")) %>%
  rowwise() %>%
  mutate(component_metas = list({
    parts <- str_split(last_name, "-")[[1]]
    metas <- unique(sapply(parts, safe_metaphone))
    setdiff(metas[metas != "" & !is.na(metas)], last_meta)
  })) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  filter(map_lgl(component_metas, ~ length(.x) > 0)) %>%
  unnest(component_metas) %>%
  mutate(last_meta = component_metas) %>%
  select(-component_metas)

indiv_filtered <- bind_rows(indiv_filtered, hyphen_rows) %>%
  mutate(.group_key = paste0(Recipient.Committee.ID, "||", last_meta))

individual_chunks <- split(indiv_filtered, indiv_filtered$.group_key)
rm(indiv_filtered, hyphen_rows)

n_chunks <- length(individual_chunks)
cat(sprintf("Processing %d (committee × last_meta) chunks...\n", n_chunks))

# flush to disk every BATCH_FLUSH chunks with results
# instead of opening the file on every iteration.
BATCH_FLUSH  <- 500L
batch_buf    <- vector("list", BATCH_FLUSH)
batch_i      <- 0L

for (i in seq_along(individual_chunks)) {
  chunk <- individual_chunks[[i]]
  if (nrow(chunk) < 2) next

  global_ids <- chunk$row_id
  chunk <- chunk %>% mutate(row_id = row_number())

  # pairs based on zip code and last name
  pairs_zip <- tryCatch(
    pair_blocking(chunk, on = c("last_meta", "zip_code_processed"), deduplication = TRUE),
    error = function(e) NULL
  )
  
  # pairs based on first initial and last name
  pairs_init <- tryCatch(
    pair_blocking(chunk, on = c("last_meta", "first_initial"), deduplication = TRUE),
    error = function(e) NULL
  )

  # score the pairs that were identified
  chunk_pairs <- bind_rows(
    if (!is.null(pairs_zip))  compare_and_score_indiv(pairs_zip,  chunk) else tibble(),
    if (!is.null(pairs_init)) compare_and_score_indiv(pairs_init, chunk) else tibble()
  )

  if (nrow(chunk_pairs) > 0) {
    chunk_pairs <- chunk_pairs %>% mutate(.x = global_ids[.x], .y = global_ids[.y])
    batch_i <- batch_i + 1L
    batch_buf[[batch_i]] <- chunk_pairs

    if (batch_i >= BATCH_FLUSH) {
      write_csv(bind_rows(batch_buf[seq_len(batch_i)]), INDIV_PAIRS_TMP, append = first_written)
      first_written <- TRUE
      batch_buf <- vector("list", BATCH_FLUSH)
      batch_i   <- 0L
    }
  }

  if (i %% 5000L == 0L) {
    cat(sprintf("  %d / %d chunks\n", i, n_chunks))
    gc(verbose = FALSE)
  }
}

# flush remaining buffer
if (batch_i > 0L) {
  write_csv(bind_rows(batch_buf[seq_len(batch_i)]), INDIV_PAIRS_TMP, append = first_written)
}
rm(individual_chunks, batch_buf)
gc(verbose = FALSE)
cat("Done. Reading pairs from disk...\n")

indiv_pairs <- if (file.exists(INDIV_PAIRS_TMP) && file.size(INDIV_PAIRS_TMP) > 0) {
  read_csv(INDIV_PAIRS_TMP, show_col_types = FALSE)
} else {
  cat("No within-committee matches found.\n")
  tibble(.x = integer(), .y = integer())
}

indiv_pairs <- indiv_pairs %>%
  group_by(.x, .y) %>%
  slice_max(score, n = 1, with_ties = FALSE) %>%
  ungroup()


# name frequency adjustment
# use stricter matching thresholds when names are common
# or when employers/orgs are uninformative
indiv_pairs <- indiv_pairs %>%
  left_join(individuals %>% select(row_id, last_name_str = last_name, first_name_str = first_name),
            by = c(".x" = "row_id")) %>%
  left_join(last_name_freq,  by = c("last_name_str"  = "last")) %>%
  left_join(first_name_freq, by = c("first_name_str" = "first")) %>%
  mutate(
    # flag whether first and last names are relatively common in the data
    common_last  = coalesce(last_name_freq,  1L) >= COMMON_LAST_MIN,
    common_first = coalesce(first_name_freq, 1L) >= COMMON_FIRST_MIN,
    common_name  = common_last & common_first,
    rare_name    = !common_last & !common_first,
    match_threshold = case_when(
      common_name & any_context_dropped ~ COMMON_NAME_STRICT,
      common_name                       ~ COMMON_NAME_THRESHOLD,
      any_context_dropped               ~ STRICT_THRESHOLD,
      TRUE                              ~ MATCH_THRESHOLD
    ),
    # unusual names flagged for review at a lower threshold 
    review_threshold = if_else(rare_name, RARE_NAME_UNCERTAIN_LOW, UNCERTAIN_LOW)
  ) %>%
  select(-last_name_str, -first_name_str, -last_name_freq, -first_name_freq)

# link tiers: auto-link vs no-link vs review
indiv_pairs <- indiv_pairs %>%
  mutate(
    link_tier = case_when(
      coalesce(first_name, 0) < FIRST_NAME_MIN ~ "no_link", # first names have to be relatively similar
      city_conflict & any_context_dropped ~ "no_link",
      common_name & city_conflict ~ "no_link",       # city disagreement is enough to reject common names
      common_name & employer_conflict ~ "no_link",   # clearly different employers also enough for common names
      score < review_threshold ~ "no_link",
      score >= match_threshold ~ "auto_link",
      TRUE                                           ~ "review"
    ),
    match_source = "internal_fuzzy"
  )

cat("Individual pairs — auto_link:", sum(indiv_pairs$link_tier == "auto_link"),
    "| review:", sum(indiv_pairs$link_tier == "review"),
    "| employer conflicts in review:", sum(indiv_pairs$employer_conflict & indiv_pairs$link_tier == "review"), "\n")

```


### Cluster individuals

Form entity clusters based on suspected matches.
Auto-links and review links are treated as true when forming clusters. 
The clusters are then used to flag which individual contributors are likely 
the same person, but used a different `Contributor.Name`.

```{r}
# treat all links as true -> name variants we be reviewed to see if they are real matches
linkable_indiv_pairs <- indiv_pairs %>% filter(link_tier %in% c("auto_link", "review"))

if (nrow(linkable_indiv_pairs) > 0) {
  g_indiv        <- graph_from_data_frame(linkable_indiv_pairs %>% select(.x, .y), directed = FALSE)
  indiv_clusters <- components(g_indiv)$membership

  indiv_cluster_raw <- tibble(row_id = as.integer(names(indiv_clusters)), cluster_num = indiv_clusters) %>%
    left_join(individuals %>% select(row_id, Contributor.Name, Contributor.ID, standardized_name,
                                     original_row_id), by = "row_id")

  indiv_cluster_uuid_map <- indiv_cluster_raw %>%
    group_by(cluster_num) %>%
    summarise(raw_names = list(unique(Contributor.Name)), .groups = "drop") %>%
    rowwise() %>%
    mutate(
      result      = list(lookup_cluster_uuid(raw_names, nem_lookup)),
      entity_id   = result$entity_id,
      is_conflict = result$is_conflict,
      is_new      = result$is_new
    ) %>%
    ungroup() %>%
    select(cluster_num, entity_id, is_conflict, is_new)

  if (any(indiv_cluster_uuid_map$is_conflict, na.rm = TRUE)) {
    cat(sprintf("WARNING: %d cluster(s) have conflicting entity registry UUIDs — check indiv_conflict_review\n",
                sum(indiv_cluster_uuid_map$is_conflict, na.rm = TRUE)))
    indiv_conflict_review <- indiv_cluster_raw %>%
      filter(cluster_num %in% indiv_cluster_uuid_map$cluster_num[indiv_cluster_uuid_map$is_conflict]) %>%
      left_join(indiv_cluster_uuid_map %>% select(cluster_num, entity_id), by = "cluster_num") %>%
      select(cluster_num, entity_id, Contributor.Name, Contributor.ID)
  }

  indiv_cluster_map <- indiv_cluster_raw %>%
    left_join(indiv_cluster_uuid_map, by = "cluster_num") %>%
    select(row_id = original_row_id, entity_id, is_conflict, is_new)
} else {
  indiv_cluster_map <- tibble(row_id = integer(), entity_id = character(),
                               is_conflict = logical(), is_new = logical())
}

# look up entity_id for unique Contributor.Name
indiv_singleton_lookup <- individuals %>%
  filter(!original_row_id %in% indiv_cluster_map$row_id) %>%
  distinct(Contributor.Name) %>%
  mutate(raw_name_key = toupper(Contributor.Name)) %>%
  left_join(nem_lookup %>% select(raw_name, entity_uuid), by = c("raw_name_key" = "raw_name")) %>%
  mutate(
    is_new    = is.na(entity_uuid),
    entity_id = coalesce(entity_uuid, UUIDgenerate(n = n()))
  ) %>%
  select(Contributor.Name, entity_id, is_new)

indiv_singletons <- individuals %>%
  filter(!original_row_id %in% indiv_cluster_map$row_id) %>% # not a part of an entity group
  select(-entity_id) %>%
  left_join(indiv_singleton_lookup, by = "Contributor.Name") %>% # join entity_id that corresponds to this name
  mutate(is_conflict = FALSE) %>%
  select(row_id = original_row_id, entity_id, is_new, is_conflict)

# auto-link only clustering: used for comparison with the method of aggregating by `Normalized` name
# NA auto_cluster means singleton or review link
auto_only_pairs <- indiv_pairs %>% filter(link_tier == "auto_link")

if (nrow(auto_only_pairs) > 0) {
  g_auto        <- graph_from_data_frame(auto_only_pairs %>% select(.x, .y), directed = FALSE)
  auto_clusters <- components(g_auto)$membership

  auto_cluster_map <- tibble(
    row_id       = as.integer(names(auto_clusters)),
    auto_cluster = auto_clusters
  ) %>%
    left_join(individuals %>% select(row_id, original_row_id), by = "row_id") %>%
    select(original_row_id, auto_cluster)
} else {
  auto_cluster_map <- tibble(original_row_id = integer(), auto_cluster = integer())
}

# within-individuals row_id to entity_id map (used by name variant queue to attach entity_id)
# indiv_pairs use within-individuals row_id; cluster_map was renamed to original_row_id
indiv_internal_to_entity <- individuals %>%
  select(row_id, original_row_id) %>%
  left_join(bind_rows(indiv_cluster_map, indiv_singletons), by = c("original_row_id" = "row_id"))

individuals_resolved <- individuals %>%
  select(-entity_id) %>%   # drop initial Normalized name-based entity_id; cluster-based wins
  left_join(bind_rows(indiv_cluster_map, indiv_singletons), by = c("original_row_id" = "row_id")) %>%
  left_join(auto_cluster_map, by = "original_row_id")

``` 

## Individual name variant review queue

For each pair surfaced by the record linkage algorithm where the two names differ, output
one row per name.

To narrow down the scope, we're only reviewing name variants of tentatively-linked entity groups
that meet the $5k threshold. Since we are not classifying entities that contributed less than 
$5k to a race, prop or PAC, tracking the name variants of these entities doesn't matter.

```{r}
# use indiv_clusters from the clustering step - includes auto-links and review links
if (exists("indiv_clusters") && length(indiv_clusters) > 0) {
  review_group_map <- tibble(
    row_id          = as.integer(names(indiv_clusters)),
    entity_group_id = paste0("igroup_", indiv_clusters)
  )
} else {
  review_group_map <- tibble(row_id = integer(), entity_group_id = character())
}

# join directly by row_id — only rows that were actually in a linked pair are included.
indiv_review_data <- review_group_map %>%
  left_join(
    individuals %>%
      select(row_id, standardized_name, Normalized, Contributor.Name, Contributor.Employer,
             Contributor.Occupation, Contributor.City,
             Contributor.State, Contributor.Zip.Code,
             Amount, Recipient.Name, Recipient.Committee.ID, Ballot.Measure,
             Office, is_pac_contribution, race_prop),
    by = "row_id"
  ) %>%
  left_join(indiv_internal_to_entity %>% select(row_id, entity_id), by = "row_id") %>%
  mutate(
    exported_name = toupper(Contributor.Name), # match the format of the names in the 2026 name map
    raw_name_key  = exported_name
  ) %>%
  add_recipient_key() %>%
  left_join(nem_lookup %>% select(raw_name, confirmed, canonical_name),
            by = c("raw_name_key" = "raw_name")) %>%
  mutate(confirmed = coalesce(confirmed, FALSE)) %>%
  group_by(entity_group_id) %>%
  filter(n_distinct(exported_name) > 1) %>% # groups with distinct Contributor.Names (multiple name variants)
  ungroup()

# all individuals contributions by Normalized × recipient — used for both queue thresholds
all_norm_recip_totals <- individuals %>%
  mutate(norm_key = coalesce(Normalized, toupper(Contributor.Name))) %>%
  add_recipient_key() %>%
  group_by(norm_key, recipient_key) %>%
  summarise(norm_total = sum(Amount, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")

# for each entity_group, identify the (`Normalized` × recipient) combos of its members,
# then pull ALL contributions sharing those `Normalized` values for those same recipients 
# (just in case one wasn't included in one of the matching pairs)

entity_group_norms_recips <- indiv_review_data %>%
  mutate(norm_key = coalesce(Normalized, toupper(Contributor.Name))) %>%
  distinct(entity_group_id, norm_key, recipient_key) # may be more than one normalized name per entity group


indiv_review_group_threshold <- entity_group_norms_recips %>%
  left_join(all_norm_recip_totals, by = c("norm_key", "recipient_key")) %>%
  group_by(entity_group_id, recipient_key) %>%
  summarise(recipient_total = sum(coalesce(norm_total, 0), na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") %>%
  group_by(entity_group_id) %>%
  summarise(max_single_recipient = max(recipient_total, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")

# flagging whether names are already in the name map or not
indiv_group_status <- indiv_review_data %>%
  group_by(entity_group_id) %>%
  summarise(
    entity_status = case_when(
      all(confirmed)  ~ "all_confirmed",
      any(confirmed)  ~ "adding_to_existing",
      TRUE            ~ "new_entity"
    ),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

# take out groups where every name pair already exists in the no-link registry (they were all reviewed already)
indiv_registry_pair_keys <- no_link_registry %>%
  filter(entity_type == "indiv") %>%
  mutate(pair_key = paste(name_a, name_b, sep = "|||")) %>%
  pull(pair_key)

indiv_group_name_pairs <- indiv_review_data %>%
  distinct(entity_group_id, name = toupper(exported_name))

indiv_fully_reviewed_groups <- indiv_group_name_pairs %>%
  inner_join(indiv_group_name_pairs, by = "entity_group_id", relationship = "many-to-many") %>%
  filter(name.x < name.y) %>%
  mutate(pair_key = paste(name.x, name.y, sep = "|||"),
         reviewed = pair_key %in% indiv_registry_pair_keys) %>%
  group_by(entity_group_id) %>%
  summarise(all_reviewed = all(reviewed), .groups = "drop") %>%
  filter(all_reviewed) %>%
  pull(entity_group_id)

# First determine which entity_groups qualify based on cluster-member analysis
qualifying_groups <- indiv_review_data %>%
  distinct(entity_group_id) %>%
  left_join(indiv_group_status, by = "entity_group_id") %>%
  left_join(indiv_review_group_threshold, by = "entity_group_id") %>%
  filter(
    entity_status != "all_confirmed",
    !entity_group_id %in% indiv_fully_reviewed_groups,
    max_single_recipient >= 5000
  )

# expand to ALL individuals sharing the same (Normalized × recipient) as any group member —
# not just cluster members - the reviewer needs every row associated with the flagged Normalized
# value in that committee, including rows that never directly matched a cluster member
indiv_queue_expanded <- entity_group_norms_recips %>%
  filter(entity_group_id %in% qualifying_groups$entity_group_id) %>%
  left_join(
    individuals %>%
      mutate(
        norm_key      = coalesce(Normalized, toupper(Contributor.Name)),
        exported_name = toupper(Contributor.Name),
        raw_name_key  = exported_name
      ) %>%
      add_recipient_key(),
    by = c("norm_key", "recipient_key")
  ) %>%
  left_join(nem_lookup %>% select(raw_name, confirmed, canonical_name),
            by = c("raw_name_key" = "raw_name")) %>%
  left_join(indiv_internal_to_entity %>% select(row_id, cluster_uuid = entity_id), by = "row_id") %>%
  mutate(confirmed = coalesce(confirmed, FALSE))

indiv_name_variant_queue <- indiv_queue_expanded %>%
  group_by(entity_group_id, exported_name, Contributor.Employer, Contributor.Occupation) %>%
  summarise(
    cluster_uuid    = first(cluster_uuid),
    canonical_name  = first(canonical_name),
    confirmed       = first(confirmed),
    n_contributions = n(),
    total_amount    = sum(Amount, na.rm = TRUE),
    city      = paste(sort(unique(Contributor.City[!is.na(Contributor.City)   & Contributor.City   != ""])), collapse = " | "),
    state     = paste(sort(unique(Contributor.State[!is.na(Contributor.State)  & Contributor.State  != ""])), collapse = " | "),
    zip       = paste(sort(unique(Contributor.Zip.Code[!is.na(Contributor.Zip.Code) & Contributor.Zip.Code != ""])), collapse = " | "),
    recipient = paste(sort(unique(recipient_key[!is.na(recipient_key) & recipient_key != ""])), collapse = " | "),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  left_join(qualifying_groups %>% select(entity_group_id, entity_status, max_single_recipient),
            by = "entity_group_id") %>%
  select(entity_group_id,
         entity_name = exported_name, cluster_uuid, canonical_name,
         entity_status, confirmed, Contributor.Employer, Contributor.Occupation,
         n_contributions, total_amount, city, state, zip, recipient, max_single_recipient)
```


```{r}
today <- format(Sys.Date(), "%m-%d-%y")
INDIV_REVIEW_OUTPUT_PATH <- paste0("08_outputs/indiv_name_variant_review_queue", today, ".csv")
write_csv(indiv_name_variant_queue, INDIV_REVIEW_OUTPUT_PATH)
cat("Individual name variant review queue:", n_distinct(indiv_name_variant_queue$entity_group_id),
    "groups,", nrow(indiv_name_variant_queue), "distinct records\n")
```



## Record linkage disambiguation queue

Surfaces cases where two records share the same `Normalized` value but are scored as
`no_link` (confirmed different people) or `review` (uncertain link). Both cases require
disambiguation: `no_link` pairs identify that records grouped together under `Normalized`
may actually be different people; `review` pairs with the same `Normalized` can't be
surfaced by the name variant queue (which requires distinct names) and need a human
decision. Applies the same $5k per-recipient threshold as the individual name variant queue.

```{r}
# no_link and review pairs where both sides share the same Normalized value
same_name_no_link <- indiv_pairs %>%
  filter(link_tier %in% c("no_link", "review")) %>%
  left_join(individuals %>% select(row_id, nm_x = Normalized), by = c(".x" = "row_id")) %>%
  left_join(individuals %>% select(row_id, nm_y = Normalized), by = c(".y" = "row_id")) %>%
  filter(!is.na(nm_x), nm_x == nm_y)

# restrict to the specific (Normalized × committee) combinations from the flagged pairs;
# pulling all committees for a flagged Normalized value incorrectly includes records that
# contributed to different recipients and were never part of any no_link pair
flagged_combos <- individuals %>%
  filter(row_id %in% unique(c(same_name_no_link$.x, same_name_no_link$.y))) %>%
  add_recipient_key() %>%
  distinct(Normalized, recipient_key)

rla_disambig_data <- individuals %>%
  add_recipient_key() %>%
  inner_join(flagged_combos, by = c("Normalized", "recipient_key")) %>%
  mutate(entity_name = toupper(Contributor.Name))

# threshold uses Normalized-level totals from all individuals (reuses all_norm_recip_totals)
rla_disambig_threshold <- rla_disambig_data %>%
  mutate(norm_key = coalesce(Normalized, toupper(Contributor.Name))) %>%
  distinct(Normalized, norm_key) %>%
  left_join(
    all_norm_recip_totals %>%
      group_by(norm_key) %>%
      summarise(max_single_recipient = max(norm_total, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop"),
    by = "norm_key"
  ) %>%
  group_by(Normalized) %>%
  summarise(max_single_recipient = max(coalesce(max_single_recipient, 0), na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") %>%
  filter(max_single_recipient >= 5000)

rla_disambig_queue <- rla_disambig_data %>%
  filter(Normalized %in% rla_disambig_threshold$Normalized) %>%
  select(
    Normalized,
    entity_name,
    entity_id,
    Contributor.Employer,
    Contributor.Occupation,
    Contributor.City,
    Contributor.State,
    Contributor.Zip.Code,
    Recipient.Committee.ID
  ) %>%
  distinct() %>%
  group_by(Normalized) %>%
  filter(n() >= 2) %>%          # remove single-profile groups — same person flagged no_link due to
  ungroup() %>%                 # common name / uninformative fields; already grouped by singleton path
  left_join(rla_disambig_threshold %>% select(Normalized, max_single_recipient),
            by = "Normalized") %>%
  mutate(in_names_map = entity_name %in% names_2026$raw_name)

# flag Normalized × committee combinations where multiple raw names are present —
# indicates name variants contributing under the same Normalized entity
committee_name_variant_flags <- rla_disambig_queue %>%
  group_by(Normalized, Recipient.Committee.ID) %>%
  summarise(has_name_variants = n_distinct(entity_name) > 1, .groups = "drop")

name_committee_totals <- rla_disambig_data %>%
  mutate(entity_name = toupper(Contributor.Name)) %>%
  group_by(entity_name, Contributor.Employer, Contributor.Occupation,
           Contributor.City, Contributor.State, Contributor.Zip.Code,
           Recipient.Committee.ID) %>%
  summarise(
    amount_to_committee = sum(Amount, na.rm = TRUE),
    n_contributions     = n(),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

rla_disambig_queue <- rla_disambig_queue %>%
  left_join(committee_name_variant_flags, by = c("Normalized", "Recipient.Committee.ID")) %>%
  left_join(name_committee_totals,
            by = c("entity_name", "Contributor.Employer", "Contributor.Occupation",
                   "Contributor.City", "Contributor.State", "Contributor.Zip.Code",
                   "Recipient.Committee.ID")) %>%
  arrange(Normalized, entity_name, Contributor.Employer, Contributor.Occupation, Contributor.City)

cat("Record linkage disambiguation queue:", n_distinct(rla_disambig_queue$Normalized),
    "Normalized groups,", nrow(rla_disambig_queue), "distinct records\n")
``` 


```{r}
today <- format(Sys.Date(), "%m-%d-%y")
DISAMBIG_REVIEW_OUTPUT_PATH <- paste0("08_outputs/individual_disambiguation_queue", today, ".csv")
write_csv(rla_disambig_queue, DISAMBIG_REVIEW_OUTPUT_PATH)
```


## Manual disambiguation review queue

Used for names I noticed while looking at the data. 

Each name in `name_list` is matched as a substring of the uppercased contributor name,
so "SMITH, STEVE" captures "SMITH, STEVE R." and "SMITH, STEVE ROBERT".

```{r}
name_list <- c(
  "SMITH, STEVE", "DAVIS, JOHN", "KING, JUSTIN", "SPENCER, RICHARD",
  "FISHER, ROBERT", "ROBERTSTON, CARL", "ROBERTSON, CHIP", "W ROBERTSON, CARL"
)

combined_pattern <- paste(toupper(name_list), collapse = "|")

manual_disambig_queue <- individuals %>%
  mutate(entity_name = toupper(Contributor.Name)) %>%
  filter(grepl(combined_pattern, entity_name)) %>%
  select(
    entity_name,
    Contributor.Employer,
    Contributor.Occupation,
    Contributor.City,
    Contributor.State,
    Contributor.Zip.Code,
    Recipient.Committee.ID,
    Recipient.Committee,
    Amount
  ) %>%
  distinct() %>%
  arrange(entity_name, Contributor.Employer, Contributor.Occupation, Contributor.City)

cat("Manual disambiguation queue:", nrow(manual_disambig_queue), "distinct records across",
    n_distinct(manual_disambig_queue$entity_name), "name variants\n")
```

```{r}
write_csv(bind_rows(manual_disambig_queue,rla_disambig_queue),"08_outputs/individual_disambiguation.csv")
```
